caption: A phone lying flat on the dashboard of a car slides forward toward the windshield when the car brakes suddenly at a red light.

sa.check: A phone lies flat on the dashboard of a car.
The car brakes suddenly at a red light.
The phone slides forward toward the windshield.
A red traffic light is visible ahead of the car.
The braking comes first and the slide follows.

pc.expect: The phone lies still while the car runs at a steady speed and starts to slide as the braking begins.
pc.fail: The phone slides while the car is still travelling steadily; or it slides with no braking visible; or it keeps sliding after the car has come to rest.

pc.expect: The slide carries the phone toward the front of the car and ends at the windshield or when the car stops.
pc.fail: The phone slides backward, away from the windshield, under braking; or it slides sideways across the dashboard while the car brakes in a straight line; or it gathers speed the longer it slides.

pc.expect: The phone keeps its face against the dashboard as it slides and stays on that surface.
pc.fail: The phone lifts off the dashboard and floats; or it stands up on edge and stays there; or it sinks into the dashboard.

pc.expect: Other loose objects in the cabin slide or swing forward at the same moment.
pc.fail: Another loose object stays put while the phone slides forward; or it slides backward under the same braking; or it moves before the braking begins.
pc.precondition: Other loose or hanging objects are visible inside the car.

pc.expect: One phone on one dashboard keeps its shape, and it stays inside the car.
pc.fail: The phone vanishes or a second one appears; or the phone passes through the windshield; or it turns into another object as it slides.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The phone's case, the dashboard and the street ahead stay consistent.
pc.fail: The phone changes colour or size; or the dashboard vents move between frames; or the traffic light shifts to another part of the scene.
